discovery: Discovery of the high-redshift galaxy population and the reconstruction of the cosmic history of star formation

nominees.name: Piero Madau
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

subfield: Astrophysics and cosmology (galaxy formation, early universe)
motivation: Until the 1990s, galaxies in the young universe were essentially invisible. Charles Steidel developed the Lyman-break technique, which turned photometric dropouts into a reliable way to find large, spectroscopically confirmed samples of star-forming galaxies at redshifts above 3. Piero Madau showed how such surveys could be combined to reconstruct the cosmic star-formation history, establishing that star formation peaked about ten billion years ago. Richard Ellis led deep spectroscopic and lensing surveys that pushed the galaxy census toward the epoch of reionization and connected galaxy assembly to the ionization of the intergalactic medium. Together their work turned 'cosmic dawn' from speculation into a quantitative, testable physical history. It set the scientific case and the methods behind Hubble's deep fields and JWST, whose observations of galaxies beyond redshift 10 now directly test the framework they built.
